pr_title: c8d/load: Don't ignore missing platform when requested
pr_body:
- replaces, closes https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/48590
- fixes https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/48589
- relates to https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/5331
- relates to https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/48295

**- What I did**
Improve `docker load` with `--platform` error when loading the requested platform failed and make it error out when the requested platform is not available after the load.

**- How to verify it**
`TestImageLoadMissing`

**- Description for the changelog**
<!--
Write a short (one line) summary that describes the changes in this
pull request for inclusion in the changelog.
It must be placed inside the below triple backticks section:
-->
```markdown changelog
containerd image store: Make `docker load --platform` return an error when the requested platform wasn't loaded.
```

**- A picture of a cute animal (not mandatory but encouraged)**

![sleepy](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae03bab6-eb45-4b35-977e-faeca74d4467)
pr_comments:
One linting failures;


```
daemon/containerd/image_exporter.go:288: File is not `goimports`-ed (goimports)
			
daemon/containerd/fake_service_test.go:7: File is not `goimports`-ed (goimports)
	"github.com/containerd/containerd/leases"
	ocispec "github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/specs-go/v1"
daemon/containerd/image_exporter_test.go:6: File is not `goimports`-ed (goimports)
	"github.com/containerd/containerd/content"
	"github.com/containerd/containerd/content/local"
```
Thanks, fixed! I think I finally got my Goland import settings right, so it should be fine now 😅

One thing I just realized is that we don't allow multiple platforms to be specified. Currently, specifying multiple platforms will result in the last one to be used;

```console
$ docker image load --platform=linux/arm64/v8 --platform=linux/riscv64 -i ./alpine2.tar
Loaded image: alpine:latest

$ docker image ls --tree
IMAGE                   ID             DISK USAGE   CONTENT SIZE   IN USE
alpine:latest           beefdbd8a1da       10.6MB         3.37MB
├─ linux/amd64          33735bd63cf8           0B             0B
├─ linux/arm/v6         50f635c8b04d           0B             0B
├─ linux/arm/v7         f2f82d424957           0B             0B
├─ linux/arm64/v8       9cee2b382fe2           0B             0B
├─ linux/386            b3e87f642f5c           0B             0B
├─ linux/ppc64le        c7a6800e3dc5           0B             0B
├─ linux/riscv64        80cde017a105       10.6MB         3.37MB
└─ linux/s390x          2b5b26e09ca2           0B             0B
```

Part of that would be the CLI, which discards multiple values if only 1 is supported; the above produces (URL-decoded);

```
/v1.48/images/load?platform={"architecture":"arm64","os":"linux","variant":"v8"}&quiet=0
```

I wonder what it would take to allow multiple platforms? My use-case here would be that I have a `image.tar` that contains (say) 8 platforms, but I only need 2 (e.g., only need arm64 and amd64). In that case, I'd want to be able to load only those.

Do we need API changes to make that possible, or would the API already be ablee to handle multiple? :thinking_face:
We didn't ship this feature yet, so there's still time to adjust the API (even if we don't support multiple yet, the API coud be able to handle it, just produce an error when multiple are passed).

```

And flakiness on Windows; I'm starting to wonder if we have some regression or if something changed on the GitHub runners; seeing `has active endpoints` errors come up various times;


```
=== FAIL: github.com/docker/docker/integration/networking TestNatNetworkICC/User_defined_nat_network (8.50s)
    nat_windows_test.go:62: assertion failed: error is not nil: Post "http://%2F%2F.%2Fpipe%2Fdocker_engine/v1.48/containers/388543970cc75202326c968cdb2544f94cf4a096072a90e20729e7182f4ab608/start": context deadline exceeded
    panic.go:626: assertion failed: error is not nil: Error response from daemon: error while removing network: network mynat id 9f8696976cb154606f63265e3f6e812855a1b9cb87f9fe268f64343240cc0485 has active endpoints
```

> one thing I did not verify is what we do with attestations; do we preserve those when saving (and loading)?

Currently we only preserve them if no `platform` was selected. Technically we _could_ also load a corresponding attestation, but I don't think we can do that with `client.Import` - we'd need a lower level code for this.

 
> Do we need API changes to make that possible, or would the API already be ablee to handle multiple? 

We can support multiple platforms with the current API via multiple `platform` query fields, like:
```
localhost/images/load?platform={"architecture":"arm64","os":"linux","variant":"v8"}&platform={"architecture":"arm","os":"linux","variant":"v5"}`
```
Tracking tickets created for various things; let's bring this one in! Thanks @vvoland !!
Removed the cherry-pick label, because this feature / flag is not yet in v27.x 🙈

issue_context.title: c8d: image load does not produce error if given platform doesn't exist
issue_context.body:
### Description

- relates to https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/5331
- relates to https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/48295


I noticed this while writing docs for https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/5331 - when specifying a `--platform` and the platform does not exist in the tar-file, no error is produced;

### Reproduce

Loading the tar without specifying a platform loads all platforms that are present in the tar;

```console
$ docker image load -i image.tar
Loaded image: alpine:latest

$ docker image ls --tree
IMAGE                   ID             DISK USAGE   CONTENT SIZE   USED
alpine:latest           beefdbd8a1da       20.6MB         11.1MB
├─ linux/s390x          2b5b26e09ca2       3.46MB         3.46MB
├─ linux/ppc64le        c7a6800e3dc5       3.57MB         3.57MB
├─ linux/arm64/v8       9cee2b382fe2       13.6MB         4.09MB
├─ linux/amd64          33735bd63cf8           0B             0B
├─ linux/arm/v6         50f635c8b04d           0B             0B
├─ linux/arm/v7         f2f82d424957           0B             0B
├─ linux/386            b3e87f642f5c           0B             0B
└─ linux/riscv64        80cde017a105           0B             0B
```

But when loading the same tar, and specifying an architecture that's not included, no error is produced;

```console
$ docker image rm alpine:latest
Untagged: alpine:latest
Deleted: sha256:beefdbd8a1da6d2915566fde36db9db0b524eb737fc57cd1367effd16dc0d06d

$ docker image load -i image.tar --platform=linux/riscv64
Loaded image: alpine:latest

$ docker image ls --tree
IMAGE           ID             DISK USAGE   CONTENT SIZE   USED
alpine:latest   beefdbd8a1da           0B             0B
```


### Expected behavior

Loading the tar should produce an error that the requested platform was not found

review_comments: As you're switching to an early return, I guess it could be before the `allImageNames` part above 😅

Silly question; would this error on "some other platform, but not the one specified is missing"?

Do we need a  "skip missing unless `<this platform>` variant? Or does the `containerd.WithImportPlatform(pm)` handle that?

The platform matcher will handle that as the non-matching platforms will be filtered out and won't be passed to the handler.
This is only needed for the `platform == nil` case, because the matcher matches **any** platform, but has a `Less` implementation that **prefers** the native one.

Wondering; should an empty `imgs` slice also return an error? I _THINK_ currently an empty `imgs` slice also will result in an empty `imageNames` slice ( "no images missing"), and because of that return "no error"
Don't think so. Empty `imgs` should probably be handled by the caller of `client.Import`. On the other hand - that would disallow loading "empty" image indexes, which we do for some tests.

Ah, right, but in the "import empty" case, would there be a "for a specific platform" constraint? (I could consider "empty" is fine if you want to "load whatever is in there", but perhaps _NOT_ if you request  a specific platform.
Perhaps adding this in a separate commit could make sense; in case we would need to backport some change to some other branch that needs it (but that change not being this PR)

Is this something that could be implemented? (e.g. a new `client.ImportAll` or something that returns both images and the index(es) ? If so, we could have a tracking ticket for that (and this comment could refer to it).
Yeah, definitely. Will create a tracking issue.

I should probably check the actual code, but was the image actually _loaded_ in this case? Will it be garbage-collected immediately after if it doesn't match what we want?

(in that case, considering if `was loaded` would potentially only add confusion, and if a shorter error would work;


```
image %s doesn't provide the requested platform (%s)
```


We could mention "contained in the archive", but not sure if that works;

```
image %s contained in the archive doesn't provide the requested platform (%s)
```

Yeah so the image will still be loaded because that's what the `client.Import` does. And we can't really delete anything after we decide that we didn't load what we wanted, because we don't know what actually got loaded and what was there before 😅

So for now this is the correct error IMO, at least unless we have a lower level import function.
This sounds like a possible tracking ticket in the making 😂 ❤️

The error message is a bit ugly with the `NotFound:` prefix, and the (somewhat) obscure "content digest ..."; I'll open a tracking ticket for that to see if we can improve that.

```console
NotFound: content digest sha256:2b5b26e09ca2856f50ac88312348d26c1ac4b8af1df9f580e5cf465fd76e3d4d: not found
```

I was hoping perhaps some trick like unwrapping it would work to clean it up, but that's stripping exactly the wrong parts, and only preserves the `not found`; 

```bash
docker load --platform linux/s390x -i alpine2.tar
requested platform (linux/s390x) found, but some content is missing: not found
```

It looks like these `NotFound:` prefixes are from gRPC; https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/12403012996e70ea4ffc4153eda4b992944bd197/vendor/google.golang.org/grpc/codes/code_string.go#L43-L44

I tried using `status.FromError()` on them to get the error-message, but that didn't work; it looks like containerd's errdefs package has a `rebaseMessage` function to do something similar and to cleanup the error, but it's either not called in our call-path, or perhaps something wrapped the error and it's discarded; https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/12403012996e70ea4ffc4153eda4b992944bd197/vendor/github.com/containerd/errdefs/grpc.go#L120-L147
